text:
maya: Heads-up — we just saw a p99 spike on hosted /v1/generate at ~11:23 UTC. p99 jumped to ~1.2s from baseline ~220ms, p95 to ~480ms. Queue depth graph looks like a backlog. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosted/api-latency
infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-api.p99 > 1.0s (11:23 UTC) — auto-sampled traces created (trace IDs attached)
sam: copying metrics now. Is this noisy-tenant or systemic? any big customer rollouts? @david any deploys in last hour?
david: no customer-facing deploys. I merged a small batching sampler tweak 35m ago (pr #4123) that slightly changes sample thresholds. might be related.
lee: grabbing kernel-selector logs from the affected nodes. quick snippet:
```
[11:22:57] kernel-selector: seq_len=768 -> selected=avx2_fallback kernel=matmul_small
[11:22:58] kernel-selector: seq_len=128 -> selected=fast_kernel kernel=matmul_prefetch
[11:23:01] kernel-selector: overload -> fallback_to_serial true; reason=coalesce_window_miss
```
lee: looks like several requests were routed to the fallback kernel (much slower) while coalescing failed due to small batch sizes.
toni: checking kvcache: hit rate dropped from 92% -> 65% between 11:12-11:24. evictions spiked.
sam: that aligns with backlog — if KV cache misses spike, runtime will regenerate KV and increase latency.
maya: can we correlate which tenant had the cache thrash? logs show eviction keys with tenant tags.
lee: filtered logs show heavy churn for tenant_id=acct-482; lots of long sequences (~700 tokens) hitting the cache and causing prefetch churn.
```
# kernel metric sample
kernel_fallback_count: 73
avg_batch_size: 2.1
coalesce_window_ms: 8
queue_depth_peak: 42
```
david: the batching sampler change reduced prefetch aggressiveness for sequences >512 to avoid overfetch. maybe an unintended side-effect: small batches + long seq -> no coalescing -> fallback kernel.
sam: can you paste the sampler diff? I want to confirm.
david: gist: changed `max_prefetch=8` -> `max_prefetch=4` for long sequences. short-term savings, hurt coalescing.
```
- if seq_len > 512: max_prefetch = 8
+ if seq_len > 512: max_prefetch = 4
```
toni: infra metrics show a noisy neighbor on the gpu-pool-12 host: tenant acct-482 had 3x request rate spike at 11:18 and used up KV cache slots quickly.
maya: so two things coincided: an aggressive tenant surge + sampler change reduced prefetch -> reduced coalescing -> fallback kernel selection -> p99 spike.
sam: quick mitigation options:
  1) rollback sampler change (david) -> should restore prefetch behavior.
  2) temporarily pin kernel selector to prefer prefetch-enabled kernels for hosted pool (lee) -> needs deploy.
  3) increase kvcache capacity on the noisy host or move tenant (oncall) -> ops.
lee: I can patch kernel-selector config to bias toward matmul_prefetch for the next 10m. Will push config via deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: Config push queued: kernel-selector.bias=matmul_prefetch -> target=hosted-pool-12
oncall: moving acct-482 off host gpu-pool-12 now to reduce noisy neighbor. evicting sessions.
```
# perf snapshot (sample)
perf top output:
  23.4%  runtime_kernel::matmul_small
  12.1%  runtime_kvcache::load
  9.6%   runtime_scheduler::coalesce
```
sam: after bias push + tenant move, p99 dropped to ~240ms within 2 minutes. queue depth back to normal. Nice.
maya: long term action items:
  - revert sampler change or rework logic so prefetch isn't reduced for seqs where coalescing benefit exists (david)
  - add an automated regression test that simulates noisy-tenant + sampler config combos (eng-ml)
  - telemetry: emit kernel-selection decision reasons to tracing so we can correlate faster (lee)
  - runtime: add a soft-limit that temporarily increases prefetch when queue_depth > X to avoid fallback (sam)
oncall: documented incident in incidents/ and assigning owner tags. mitigation complete. marking as monitor-for-1h :eyes:
maya: thanks everyone. please post PR links and postmortem notes here when ready :thumbsup:
